text:
On 24 September, Bitget disclosed a security incident.

If you hold funds on any exchange, you know what happens next.

You open the app. Check your balance. Then you start wondering what’s actually sitting behind the number on your screen.

That question is fair.

So I looked at what Bitget has published since.

According to Bitget’s latest Proof of Reserves snapshot, dated 29 September 2026 at 17:00 UTC+8, the reported overall reserve ratio is 131%, with all 19 covered assets above the 100% benchmark.

A few of the reported ratios:

BTC: 142%
ETH: 110%
USDT: 107%
USDC: 154%
SOL: 157%
BNB: 104%

Bitget states that user account balances were unaffected and that the incident has been contained. Its forensic investigation, fund tracing and recovery work remain ongoing.

The part worth paying attention to is the verification.

Bitget provides a Merkle Tree-based system that allows users to check whether their own included balance is reflected in the published data, without exposing personal information or other users’ balances.

So don’t just take my word for it.

Check the data yourself.

A PoR snapshot is a point-in-time disclosure covering specific assets. It is not a guarantee and does not remove market, operational, custody or trading risk. It is also separate from the User Protection Fund.

Official PoR page:
https://t.co/0k8oXiJA06

Paid partnership with Bitget. Not financial advice. Crypto carries high risk. DYOR.

.@NucleusCodes put a @zerufinance campaign on two boards at once. 
The contribution side splits a token pool among the top 300 and attaches one GTD Zerus spot to each of those winners. 
The reputation side splits 870 GTD spots among the top 700, with higher ranks receiving more. 
Output therefore bundles a token share with access, while history stays an access layer only. 
The same profile can sit on both doors, but the prize type changes with the door. What you produce and who you already are are packed separately. Distribution is a two-output ranking, not one bucket.
